questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: A written accent on a word whose last syllable is stressed
questions.learningObjective: Apply the rule for a final-stressed word
questions.stem: In interpreting a graph of stress patterns, which final-stressed word takes a written accent under the general rule?

options.text: A word ending in a consonant other than n or s with stress on the last syllable
A word ending in n or s with stress on the last syllable
options.misconception: confuses the n-s exception with the rule

options.text: A word ending in a vowel with stress on the last syllable
A one-syllable word with stress on its only syllable

questions.explanation: Final-stressed words take an accent only when they end in a consonant other than n or s. Vowel and n-s endings are exempt, and monosyllables follow other rules.

questions.stem: In interpreting a graph of syllable counts, explain why a diphthong counts as one syllable in the accent test.

answer.exemplar: A diphthong counts as one syllable because the two vowels form a single vocalic nucleus, so the stress position is counted as one unit.

questions.explanation: The diphthong's vowels form one nucleus, so it counts as one syllable. Counting them separately would misplace the stress.

options.text: No, because all final-stressed words are exempt

questions.explanation: Words ending in n or s are exempt from the final-stress accent. The exemption is specific to those endings, not all words.

questions.stem: In interpreting that graph, does that word take an accent?

options.text: No, because y counts as a vowel
Yes, because y counts as a consonant
No, because y-ended words are exempt

questions.explanation: y counts as a consonant, so a final-stressed y-ended word takes an accent. It is not exempt or conditional.
